title: Gnocchi al Gorgonzola
subtitle: Potato gnocchi in a creamy gorgonzola sauce
excerpt: Shop-bought or homemade potato gnocchi in a quick, rich gorgonzola cream sauce. Ready in under 20 minutes and impressive enough for company. The gorgonzola melts into the cream and clings to every pillow of gnocchi.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gnocchi al gorgonzola is a northern Italian dish, particularly associated with the Lombard and Piedmontese cooking traditions where Gorgonzola, one of Italy's oldest cheeses, originates. Gorgonzola is produced in Piedmont and Lombardy and is named after the town of Gorgonzola near Milan. The creamy blue cheese sauce is one of the simplest and most popular ways to serve gnocchi in the northern Italian tradition.

content.text: Gorgonzola melts readily into warm cream without any need for vigorous cooking. Keep the sauce over very low heat and add the cheese gradually, stirring as it melts in. Do not let the sauce boil after the cheese is added or it can split and become grainy. The gnocchi should go straight from the boiling water into the sauce while hot.
Bring a large pan of salted water to a boil for the gnocchi.

In a wide frying pan over low heat, melt the butter. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the cream and warm gently. Add the gorgonzola and stir until melted and smooth. Season with pepper and a tiny pinch of salt (the cheese is already salty).

Cook the gnocchi in the boiling water until they float, plus 30 seconds more. Scoop out with a slotted spoon and add directly to the sauce. Toss gently to coat. Add a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
Serve in warm bowls, scattered with parmesan, black pepper, and walnuts if using.
